graders.name: 03-finding-cites-contradicted-source-point
graders.evidence:
## Verdict
- changes required
- Blocking findings: 1

## Findings
- P1
  - Category: conflict
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md section 2 (Scope, bullet 1), and section 3 (AC-01, AC-02)
  - Evidence: fixtures/source-notes.md point 4 states the coordinator role's existing case "was left untouched — no new case was added for it in this batch, and it does not pair a planted defect with a control section the way the three new cases do." Point 5 confirms the defect/control pairing applies only to "each of the three new cases." fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md section 2 claims "This batch adds one seeded-defect eval case for each of the four reviewer roles — code, security, document and coordinator — pairing each planted defect with a correct control section in the same fixture," and AC-01/AC-02 both require behavior for "each of the four cases." This is a scope/count claim the source does not support and directly contradicts.
  - Suggestion: Change section 2 to state three new cases (code, security, document), explicitly note the coordinator role's case is unchanged and out of scope for this batch, and revise AC-01/AC-02 to read "Each of the three new cases..." so a builder does not write a grader for a fourth, nonexistent case.

## Not raised
- Scope bullet 1's coverage of the code-reviewer case traces to source-notes.md point 1.
- Scope bullet 1's coverage of the security-reviewer case traces to source-notes.md point 2.
- Scope bullet 1's coverage of the document-validator case traces to source-notes.md point 3.
- Scope bullet 2 (fixtures copied by each case's own scaffold.sh, invoked only with `--scaffold`) matches source-notes.md point 6 exactly.
- AC-01 and AC-02, apart from the "four cases" count, state observable pass/fail conditions (positive grader detects the defect; negative grader confirms the control is not flagged) — not weak criteria.
- No ambiguous sentence found: each requirement admits one reading.
- Identifiers (AC-01, AC-02) are unique and sequentially numbered; no duplication or misfiled section found.

## Evidence
- Files read: fixtures/source-notes.md, fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md.
- No previous review report found at fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md.review.md; treated as round 1.
- All six categories (gaps, ambiguities, conflicts, excesses, weak criteria, organization) were checked against the full source-to-document map; only the conflict above was found.

graders.name: 03-finding-cites-contradicted-source-point
graders.evidence:
## Verdict
- changes required
- Blocking findings: 1

## Findings
- P1
  - Category: conflict
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md section 2 (Scope), lines 15–17; propagated into section 3, AC-01 (lines 23–24) and AC-02 (lines 25–26)
  - Evidence: The document states "This batch adds one seeded-defect eval case for each of the four reviewer roles — code, security, document and coordinator — pairing each planted defect with a correct control section in the same fixture," and both AC-01 and AC-02 require this of "each of the four cases." fixtures/source-notes.md point 4 states the opposite for coordinator: "The `coordinator` role's existing case (`coordinator-explore-then-ask`) was left untouched — no new case was added for it in this batch, and it does not pair a planted defect with a control section the way the three new cases do." The source supports three new cases (code, security, document — points 1–3), not four, and explicitly says the coordinator case has neither a new planted defect nor a control pairing.
  - Suggestion: Correct Scope to state the batch adds one new seeded-defect eval case for each of the three reviewer roles — code, security and document — each pairing a planted defect with a control section, and separately note that the coordinator role's existing case is left untouched and out of scope for this batch. Rewrite AC-01 and AC-02 to read "each of the three new cases," and drop or replace any acceptance criterion that would require the coordinator's existing case to have a positive/negative grader for a planted defect it does not contain.
  - Reported by: claude

## Not raised
- Scope bullet 1's phrase "pairing each planted defect with a correct control section in the same fixture" is otherwise sourced to source-notes.md point 5 ("a keyword-only reviewer risks flagging the control too"), correct for the three new cases.
- Scope bullet 2 (lines 18–19), on fixtures being copied by each case's own `scaffold.sh` invoked only with `--scaffold`, traces exactly to source-notes.md point 6.
- The Goal statement is a faithful generalization of source-notes.md and introduces no unsourced requirement (excess check held).
- AC-01 and AC-02, apart from the "four vs three" count, are each observably pass/fail (grader present/absent, control correctly unflagged) — no weak-criterion defect beyond what P1 already covers.
- No sentence in the document produced two materially different builder readings (ambiguity check held).
- Identifiers AC-01 and AC-02 are unique, sequential, and filed under the correct section (organization check held); no duplicate or misplaced identifiers found.
- Source-notes.md points 1–3 (code-reviewer-form-check, security-reviewer-authz-check, document-validator-overclaim-check) each trace to the "code, security, document" portion of Scope bullet 1 — the roles named there, apart from the erroneous inclusion of coordinator, are correct.

## Evidence
- Files read: fixtures/source-notes.md (source, 11 lines), fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md (document under review, 31 lines).
- No previous review report exists at fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md.review.md; this is treated as round 1.
- All six categories (gaps, ambiguities, conflicts, excesses, weak criteria, organization) were checked against the full source-to-document map built from source-notes.md points 1–6 and PRD sections 1–4.
- No project language file was consulted; report written in English per the shared contract's default.

graders.evidence:
## Verdict
- changes required
- Blocking findings: 2

## Findings
- P1
  - Category: conflict
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md, section 2 "Scope", first bullet ("This batch adds one seeded-defect eval case for each of the four reviewer roles — code, security, document and coordinator...")
  - Evidence: fixtures/source-notes.md point 4 states the coordinator role's existing case (`coordinator-explore-then-ask`) "was left untouched — no new case was added for it in this batch, and it does not pair a planted defect with a control section the way the three new cases do." Only three seeded-defect cases were added (points 1–3: code, security, document); the coordinator role got no new case at all.
  - Suggestion: Rewrite the bullet to state that this batch adds one seeded-defect eval case each for the code, security and document reviewer roles, each pairing a planted defect with a correct control section in the same fixture; separately note that the coordinator role's existing case was left untouched and does not have this planted-defect/control-section pairing.
  - Reported by: claude
- P2
  - Category: conflict
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md, section 3 "Acceptance criteria", AC-01 and AC-02 ("Each of the four cases has a positive grader that detects the planted defect" / "...a negative grader confirming its control section is not wrongly flagged")
  - Evidence: fixtures/source-notes.md point 4 establishes the coordinator's existing case has no planted defect and no paired control section, unlike the three new cases (point 5). A builder following AC-01/AC-02 as written would try to build a positive grader detecting a "planted defect" and a negative grader for a "control section" on the coordinator case, neither of which exists per the source.
  - Suggestion: Scope AC-01 and AC-02 to the three new cases (`code-reviewer-form-check`, `security-reviewer-authz-check`, `document-validator-overclaim-check`); if the coordinator's existing case needs any verification, state a separate criterion reflecting that it has no planted defect or control-section pairing.
  - Reported by: claude
